title: Trastuzumab IV · weekly · metastatic

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Attend planned echoes. Report breathlessness, ankle swelling, rapid weight gain or infusion symptoms.

purpose: Weekly trastuzumab targets HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer to help control it. Review symptoms, treatment benefit and cardiac function regularly.
schedule_summary: IV trastuzumab every 7 days, continuing while beneficial and tolerated. This weekly NCCP card is for metastatic disease, without a fixed one-year course.

safety_note: New breathlessness, chest pain, collapse, severe allergic symptoms or sudden serious illness need urgent assessment on any day.
teachback: What is the purpose of your treatment? Which heart or blood test is due next, and which team arranges and reviews it?
consent_support: Discuss expected benefit, alternatives, route, duration, cardiac monitoring, pregnancy / contraception, urgent contacts and individual treatment risks. Add any companion drug using its own regimen information.
urgent_extra: Report breathlessness, swelling, rapid weight gain, palpitations or persistent diarrhoea; tell staff immediately about a reaction during treatment.

support.title: Support for this medicine
support.text: Trastuzumab alone has minimal emetogenic risk. Routine chemotherapy antiemetics, steroids and growth factors are not added automatically. Previous reactions require a separate plan.

support.title: Blood and heart appointments
support.text: Baseline FBC, renal and liver profile; repeat blood tests according to the team / companion-regimen plan (NCCP does not assign a universal interval here). Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C13 for an uninterrupted weekly course.

support.title: Other treatments
support.text: Any companion medicine, local procedure or radiotherapy needs its own oncology plan. This weekly metastatic component card does not prescribe an early-breast surgical sequence.

support.title: Pregnancy / contraception
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and contraception before treatment. Report pregnancy promptly; do not breastfeed during treatment or for 7 months afterwards. The team confirms the medicine-specific contraception duration.

questions.q: How long will I receive treatment?
questions.a: IV trastuzumab every 7 days, continuing while beneficial and tolerated. This weekly NCCP card is for metastatic disease, without a fixed one-year course.
Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C13 for an uninterrupted weekly course. Existing HER2 exposure and delays affect cycle numbering; the team should give the actual due window.
Radiotherapy is used for a defined site or symptom when indicated. The oncology and radiation teams agree whether this medicine continues or pauses; do not infer a concurrent schedule from this card.

questions.q: Does a tumour marker replace a scan?
questions.a: No. In metastatic disease it may add information to symptoms and imaging. It should not alone determine treatment changes. In symptom-free early disease it is not routine recurrence screening.

questions.q: Why was this treatment chosen for me?
questions.a: This weekly intravenous treatment targets HER2-positive breast cancer that has spread. Your team considers previous treatment, current cancer control, side effects and heart health when deciding whether to continue or change it. The weekly and three-weekly schedules have different doses and visit patterns. Ask why the weekly schedule fits your plan and whether this card covers one part of a wider treatment combination. There is no automatic one-year stopping point for this metastatic pathway.

items.text: This card describes trastuzumab. Pertuzumab, taxanes, endocrine medicines and antibody–drug conjugates require their own treatment instructions.

chapters.title: Before treatment and between visits
chapters.intro: The team should arrange and review the tests.

items.title: Blood checks
items.text: Baseline FBC, renal and liver profile; repeat blood tests according to the team / companion-regimen plan (NCCP does not assign a universal interval here)

items.title: Cardiac checks
items.text: Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C13 for an uninterrupted weekly course. Baseline cardiac assessment includes ECG in EMA trastuzumab information. Further ECGs follow symptoms / cardiac plan; an ECG does not replace an echo.

items.title: After stopping
items.text: EMA trastuzumab information: cardiac assessment every 6 months after stopping, until 24 months; after anthracyclines in early disease, yearly to 5 years or longer if function falls.

chapters.title: The wider pathway
chapters.intro: Coordinate cancer medicines with local treatment and follow-up.

items.title: Scans and markers
items.text: Response imaging commonly every 2–4 months, adapted to sites, disease course and treatment. A new symptom can need earlier imaging. Tumour markers may supplement assessment, never determine a treatment change alone.

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: Radiotherapy is used for a defined site or symptom when indicated. The oncology and radiation teams agree whether this medicine continues or pauses; do not infer a concurrent schedule from this card.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is planned, assess fracture risk and DEXA need. Repeat timing depends on results and bone treatment; this is not an automatic HER2-therapy scan.

steps.title: Before your visit
steps.text: Confirm the dose, symptoms, required blood results and echo due window.

steps.title: Access and administration
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used according to the treatment plan. A port insertion is a separate procedure.

steps.title: Treatment and observation
steps.text: First infusion usually 90 minutes; later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated. NCCP observation is 6 hours from the start of the first infusion and 2 hours from the start of later infusions; ask about the unit’s approved policy.

steps.title: After the visit
steps.text: Tell the unit how late the dose is. A delay over one week can require re-loading after clinician review; do not assume every continuation visit needs a loading dose. This medicine does not routinely require a take-home pump.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: First infusion usually 90 minutes; later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated. NCCP observation is 6 hours from the start of the first infusion and 2 hours from the start of later infusions; ask about the unit’s approved policy.

details.title: Missed or delayed visit
details.text: Tell the unit how late the dose is. A delay over one week can require re-loading after clinician review; do not assume every continuation visit needs a loading dose.

monitoring_schedule.title: When your checks happen
monitoring_schedule.note: Cycle examples assume no delays and count from the first dose of this schedule. If switching route or continuing previous HER2 treatment, preserve the existing echo due date. Tests are scheduled by elapsed time and clinical need; the team owns booking and result review. NCCP remains 12-weekly during treatment, including maintenance; a longer interval needs an explicit individual specialist plan.
